title: Isolation Precautions (PPE Donning & Doffing)
summary: Proper sequence for applying and removing personal protective equipment (PPE).
steps: DONNING (putting on):
1. Perform hand hygiene.
2. Put on gown — tie at neck and waist.
3. Put on mask or respirator — ensure proper fit/seal for N95.
4. Put on eye protection.
5. Put on gloves — pull over gown cuffs.
DOFFING (removing — most contaminated items first):
1. Remove gloves: grasp outside of one glove, peel off. Hold in gloved hand. Slide finger under clean cuff of other glove, peel off over first glove. Discard.
2. Perform hand hygiene.
3. Remove gown: untie, pull from neck and shoulders, roll away from body, discard.
4. Perform hand hygiene.
5. Remove eye protection — handle by the arms/headband, not the front.
6. Remove mask — handle by straps only, do not touch front.
7. Perform hand hygiene immediately.
nursing_considerations: Contact: gloves + gown (MRSA, C. diff, VRE).
Droplet: gloves + gown + surgical mask + eye protection (influenza, COVID, RSV).
Airborne: gloves + gown + N95 + eye protection — negative pressure room required (TB, measles, varicella).
C. diff requires soap and water hand hygiene — alcohol gel is NOT effective against spores.
Perform hand hygiene at every step of doffing to prevent self-contamination.

title: Hand Hygiene (Medical & Surgical)
summary: Performing WHO-5-moment and routine hand hygiene with soap/water or alcohol-based hand rub (ABHR) to prevent infection transmission.
equipment: Soap and water sink with paper towels
steps: WHO 5 Moments — perform hand hygiene:
1. Before touching a patient.
2. Before a clean/aseptic procedure.
3. After body fluid exposure risk.
4. After touching a patient.
5. After touching patient surroundings.
Alcohol-Based Hand Rub (ABHR) — 20–30 seconds:
Apply enough product to cover all surfaces (typically 1–2 pumps).
Rub palm to palm, interlace fingers, rub backs of hands, clean thumbs in circular motion, rub fingertips into opposite palm, rub wrists.
Continue until completely dry — do not wipe off.
Soap and Water — 40–60 seconds (required when: hands visibly soiled, after C. diff contact, before eating, after restroom use):
Wet hands. Apply soap.
Lather vigorously for at least 20 seconds — all surfaces including between fingers, backs of hands, thumbs, and nails.
Rinse thoroughly under running water.
Dry with single-use paper towel.
Use towel to turn off faucet — avoid recontaminating clean hands.
Surgical Hand Scrub (pre-operative, 3–5 minutes):
Remove jewelry. Use nail pick under each nail first.
Apply antimicrobial scrub solution (CHG or povidone-iodine). Brush nails for 30 seconds each hand.
Scrub palms, backs of hands, fingers, wrists, and forearms to 2 inches above elbow.
Rinse, keeping hands above elbows. Dry with sterile towel.
nursing_considerations: ABHR is preferred for routine clinical hand hygiene — it is faster, less irritating, and more effective than soap/water for most pathogens.
Soap and water is mandatory after C. difficile contact — spores are resistant to ABHR.
Rings, watches, and artificial nails harbor more bacteria — remove before patient care when possible.
Compliance with hand hygiene is the single most effective measure to prevent healthcare-associated infections (HAIs).
After 5+ applications of ABHR, wash with soap and water — build-up of emollients can decrease antimicrobial effectiveness.

title: Sterile Field Setup & Maintenance
summary: Establishing and maintaining a sterile field for aseptic procedures such as catheterization, wound care, and IV insertion.
equipment: Sterile NS or sterile water (if needed)
steps: Prepare a clean, dry, flat surface for the sterile field.
Inspect sterile packages: check expiration date, package integrity, and moisture (wet packaging = no longer sterile).
Open the outer wrapper of the sterile drape/towel: open away from the body, drop contents onto clean surface without touching the inside of the package.
The sterile field is considered contaminated within a 1-inch border around all edges — work inside this border only.
Don sterile gloves AFTER the sterile field is set up (to prevent contamination from package opening).
Add sterile supplies: open sterile packages and flip or drop contents onto field without contaminating sterile gloves or the field.
Pour sterile solutions: hold bottle label facing up, open away from the field. Pour from about 4–6 inches above the sterile container on the field. Do not let bottle touch the field.
Maintain line-of-sight with the sterile field at all times — never turn your back on it.
Keep sterile field at waist level or above — below-waist level is considered contaminated.
If any portion of the sterile field is contaminated (touched by non-sterile item, splashed, breached), replace that item or discard the field entirely.
A sterile field becomes contaminated when: wet, touched by non-sterile item, left unattended, taken below waist level, or if sterility of any item is in doubt.
nursing_considerations: When in doubt, throw it out — never proceed with a questionable sterile field.
Talking, sneezing, or coughing over a sterile field contaminates it — wear a mask and minimize talking.
Sterile gloves do NOT protect the field from your reaching over it — stay on the sterile field side.
Open-package technique: contents always go ONTO the field (flipped or dropped). Never reach across a sterile field with a non-sterile arm.
Time matters: the longer a sterile field is left open, the higher the risk of contamination by airborne particles.
